tasks.task: Review a page, screen or flow for usability

items.when: When you review a flow step by step as a named user and rank each problem by severity
When the client wants a quick score out of 100 with each usability break and ranked fixes
When people cannot tell what is clickable or what just happened after they act
When people stall at a choice, to find where layout, defaults or order stop them
When the review should end with a one-morning test with three people
When the screen makes people stop and think about what to do next

tasks.task: Walk through a flow as three types of user

items.when: Before the walkthrough, to turn research notes into the user types and their paths
When you want to see what a visitor thinks at each scroll and where they doubt or leave
When each user type must be taken through the flow step by step with severity ratings
When all three user types look alike, to ask who cannot take part at all

tasks.task: Plan a small usability test for one flow

items.when: When you have a prototype or live flow and want to watch real people try it
When the test must fit one morning, with tasks, a script and a fix list
When you also need moderator notes and a findings summary format
When the test is part of getting a flow ready for development

tasks.task: Check a prototype before user testing

items.when: Before sessions, to find test blockers and reword any task that leads the user
When a new flow is about to go to development and must be tested first
Before recruiting anyone, to fix the obvious problems so sessions find the hidden ones
When there is no prototype yet and you need a clickable one to test

tasks.task: Turn test sessions or complaints into ranked findings

items.when: When sessions are done and you need problems, how many hit each one and fixes
When you have interviews, surveys or tickets and need themes ranked with quotes
When the input is complaints, to get a theme map and ranked design questions
When one loud voice may be skewing the list, to rank by what most users need
When there are many transcripts and you need to ask questions across them

tasks.task: Turn a design review into a fix list developers can act on

items.when: When you have one screen or prototype and need issues, a revised brief and a test
When new screens arrive often, to get a ready, fix-first or rethink call on each
When the input is a mockup or Figma link and you want hierarchy and consistency notes
When the fix list is long and the team must pick what fits the next sprint

tasks.task: Write a text wireframe spec for an app or flow

items.when: Before the screens, to map the steps, choices, error states and drop-off points
When the flow is open, to get a second route built on proven patterns to compare
When a feature list must become a screen list, flow map and per-screen spec in words
When you want text wireframes at three levels of detail for different screen sizes
When a screen has only its happy path, to add empty, loading, error and offline
When a screen gives no cue about what to do or no feedback after an action
When the spec is drafted, to walk it as a first-time user before anyone builds it

tasks.task: Write text wireframes for a small website

items.when: Before any page, to agree the page tree and menu from what visitors come to do
When each page needs its one job, layout zones and exact words written out
When you want a rough version first to compare page layouts before the detail
When a page is drafted, to check hierarchy, spacing and how it works on mobile

tasks.task: Write a component spec sheet for an interface

items.when: When one component needs variants, states, accessible behaviour and tokens in a brief
When the components come from the screens and need exact labels and behaviour
Before handoff, to find the states and variants still missing

tasks.task: Plan a site structure, main menu, footer and mobile menu

items.when: When the site grew without a plan, to mark each page keep, merge, redirect or delete
When you rank top tasks, group pages by task and write labels in visitors' words
When you want a second page tree with a URL and internal link plan to compare
When the site is a store and the menu depends on collections and filters
When the menu is drafted, to rate each label and rewrite the unclear ones

tasks.task: Audit and fix navigation and labels on a live site

items.when: When visitors cannot find key pages or the team is arguing about the menu
When the client asks what similar sites do, to set the bar their menu must meet
When you have the current menu, to score each choice out of 100
When labels use internal terms, to rewrite them in the words users already say

tasks.task: Plan a findability test for a menu or page tree

items.when: Before the test, to list the top tasks people must be able to find
When you write neutral find-it tasks and decide who to recruit
When the test must be run in one morning with a few people and a script

tasks.task: Write or fix the microcopy on a screen or form

items.when: When buttons, labels, hints and confirmations must say what happens and what to do next
When you want a second set of labels and messages in a friendlier voice to compare
When the text uses company terms, to swap in users' own words and read it aloud
When a line is too long for its space and every word seems needed
When the labels are written, to rate whether each choice is clear before a click

tasks.task: Write error and empty-state messages for a flow

items.when: When you have the screens and current text and need every state listed and reworded
When you have a list of error messages that blame the user or say nothing useful
When a hard moment needs a calm message, to write two or three versions to choose from
When errors are shown by colour alone or are not tied to the field they refer to

tasks.task: Design first-use onboarding and write its copy

items.when: Before rewriting, to find the step between sign-up and first use that loses most people
When you know the product's first win and need a flow that cuts set-up to reach it
When a guided set-up may work better, to compare a wizard with skip options
When each onboarding step needs its title, one line of help and a button label
When the product has changed, to check each instruction still matches the screen

tasks.task: Write a product voice and terminology guide

items.when: When the brand's voice lives in documents and calls, to draw the rules out first
When several people write interface text and need shared words and tone
When new text is written, to find where it breaks the guide, with before and after
When one thing may have two names across the product, to catch every clash

tasks.task: Make a long form, sign-up or checkout easier to finish

items.when: When a form is long, to get a shorter field list, a new flow and a test script
When sign-up loses people, to cut fields and make each step's copy clearer
When one long page may work better in stages, to compare a stepped version
When every team wants its own field kept and nobody will cut one
When the flow is a checkout, to rank fixes for guest checkout, fields and surprise costs
When the new form is drafted, to walk it step by step before it is built

tasks.task: Check a flow for deceptive design

items.when: Before launching a sign-up, checkout, cancel or consent flow, or when asked to make leaving harder
When a trick is removed and the team needs an honest way to make the same case
When it is unclear whether a nudge uses real proof and limits or invented pressure
When the flow includes AI answers, to add trust checks to the review

tasks.task: Run a quick accessibility check on a screen or page

items.when: Before a design is signed off or a page goes live, to catch the common problems early
When you can point at the page or code and want ranked problems with fixes
When the client needs gaps listed by level and notes for an accessibility statement
When the quick check finds a lot, to plan keyboard and screen reader tests

tasks.task: Plan user interviews or research for one question

items.when: When you know what you need to learn but not which research method fits
When the method is interviews and you need recruiting, a guide and synthesis steps
When the question is why people use the product at all, to frame it as jobs

tasks.task: Map personas and the user journey from research

items.when: When you have raw interviews or tickets and need the patterns and users' own words
When research notes must become personas, a path map and a test plan
When each step needs its touchpoints, friction and the systems behind it
When a finding must become a short story the team can design and test against

tasks.task: Find where users leave a flow and prove the fix works

items.when: When new users leave early and you need the leak, one fix and a way to measure it
When you have an event log, to see conversion and drop-off at each step
When the fix will be tested, to set sample size and stop rules before launch
When test data is in, to check the split and make a ship call with a range

tasks.task: Design a chatbot or AI assistant flow

items.when: When a chatbot needs its questions, error recovery and fallbacks mapped
When the screen is chat-first, to see a version with few controls and clear outcomes
When the assistant can act, to set which actions need a person to approve
When the flow is drafted, to check it against named principles and AI trust checks

always.when: Before writing product words that must match the client's live site and voice
Before a spec or copy deck is sent, to catch typos and terms used two ways

helpers.when: When the flow is agreed and the screens need type, colour, spacing and states
When the product needs a full audit against the standard, not a quick check
When the job needs a larger study: many interviews, a survey or a segment analysis
When drop-off must be measured from event data before and after the fix
When the wireframes or copy must be built or the fix list applied in code
When the page is a sales or landing page and the words must sell, not only guide

gaps: No library item plans a card sort, tree test or first-click test; only the kit's general test plan covers findability
No library item checks a flow for deceptive design or dark patterns, or designs a fair cookie consent banner; only the kit prompt does
No library item audits buttons and labels across a whole product; the label checker works on one menu or screen
No library item checks the reading level of interface text
No library item plans the structure of an app: sections, tabs and where each feature lives
No library item turns a text wireframe into a picture or clickable draft to show a client
No library item writes a recruiting screener, consent form or note-taking sheet for test sessions
No library item writes push, in-app or system notification copy
No library item designs on-site search: results, filters and no-results pages
